To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a memory-side cache can achieve near-optimal bandwidth utilization when it is dynamically partitioned between the cache and the main memory based on a light-weight learning algorithm.

(1) a memory-side cache should not always be used to maximize its hit rates, but should instead exploit the available bandwidth, and (2) a simple learning-based access partitioning algorithm can achieve near-optimal performance in this regard.

(i) a memory-side DRAM can be effectively used as a cache to improve the system performance, and (ii) the memory-side DRAM needs to be partitioned between cache and main memory to exploit under-utilization of the main memory bandwidth.

the traditional approach of maximizing hit rate in the memory-side cache can be counter-productive.
